newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta exchange unaffected by election outcome.
newsitem.headline: Malta exchange unaffected by election outcome.

text.p: The Malta stock exchange on Wednesday appeared unaffected by the change of government following the election of the Labour Party, which opposes privatisation of state-owned companies.
The share index rose by 0.8 percent to 1,023.10. Turnover in the once-weekly trading session reached just over Lm 145,670 ($404,962) from Lm 209,707 ($582,985) the week before.
There were 61 deals, of which 38 were in equities and 23 in fixed income securities.

Business in equities amounted to just over Lm 61,870 with 50,196 shares transacted. Of these, 38,746 were Bank of Valletta shares transacted in 24 deals for an average of 131 cents per share, up two cents.
There was only one deal in Mid-Med Bank, with 1,000 shares being transacted for 153 cents per share, up just over one cent.
In Lombard Bank Malta, 3,700 shares changed hands for an average 150.7 cents per share, up just four cents.

A total of 6,700 ordinary shares in Simonds Farsons Cisk sold for an average 52 cents per share, unchanged. The market also saw 50 Farsons six percent preference shares 2001/3 selling for an average Lm10.58. These shares were last traded on September 18 at the same price.

In the government bond market, 10 issues were dealt in, turnover reaching just under Lm 83,800. Business was mainly in the seven percent MGS 2006, 6.75 percent 2001 (III) and the 7.5 percent MGS 2011.

The stock exchange said the following government stocks have now been admitted to the official list: 6.3 percent MGS 1999 (V) and 7.5 percent MGS 2011, totalling Lm20.25 million. Trading in those securities started on Wednesday.
